newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New Zealand signs veterinary accord with EU.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand signs veterinary accord with EU.

text.p: New Zealand signed an accord with the European Union on Tuesday on the mutual recognition of veterinary and plant health standards, the first state to do so.
The accord, agreed by all EU states except Finland, which abstained, was signed on the margins of a meeting of EU farm ministers.

The agreement, following on measures agreed in the GATT Uruguay round creating stricter sanitary and phytosanitary measures, begins on January 1, when EU states are scheduled to implement it within the framework of the single market. This will involve harmonising import rules in the 15 member states.

It is the first stage in an EU drive to create formal regulations with its major trading partners, but New Zealand is sole country to have signed an accord since the end of round table talks on December 6.
Trading partners including the United States, Canada, Australia and Argentina are unlikely to sign by the Jan 1, 1997 deadline.

But an Irish EU presidency official said last week that providing sufficient progress is made, other partners were likely to reach a "gentleman's agreement" with the EU, extending current import arrangements for up to three months.
